title: Ten-round structural diffusion for 38- and 40-branch type-II GFNs
summary: Determine whether even--odd branch permutations on 38 and 40 branches can reach full forward and inverse structural diffusion in ten rounds.

formal_statement.body: For each $k\in\{19,20\}$, let $\Omega_k=\{0,\ldots,2k-1\}$ and initialize dependency sets by $D_j^{(0)}=\{j\}$. Update them by unioning the two branches of each type-II Feistel pair before applying an even--odd permutation $\pi_k$. Define $\operatorname{DR}(\pi_k)$ as the maximum of the first round at which every dependency set equals $\Omega_k$ for $\pi_k$ and for $\pi_k^{-1}$. Do permutations $\pi_{19}$ and $\pi_{20}$ exist with $\operatorname{DR}(\pi_{19})=\operatorname{DR}(\pi_{20})=10$?

scope.domain: Structural diffusion in type-II Generalised Feistel Networks
assumptions: Forward and inverse directions both count
scope.unresolved_remainder: The record consolidates the 38- and 40-branch instances. The 42-branch case, active-S-box security, and classification of all optimal permutations remain outside this record's scope.

progress.summary: The source paper proved that nine rounds are impossible for the relevant sizes and posed the ten-round witness challenge for 38 and 40 branches.
